Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with very itchy, sore, red skin for a few days.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: Yes. So, it's been a few days now. I have like a sore, and a red skin. It's kind of, it's really itchy, and it's like super annoying.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Rash is located on the chest, hands, and inside the elbows.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Uh, no. Just the chest, hands and like, like inside the elbows. Yeah.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Itching is severe enough to cause insomnia.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I can't even sleep at night.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Itching interferes with concentration at work.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: even at work I, I can, when I'm in a meeting and I have to, like uh think about my work, I can't focus, I can't actually focus on my work.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Onset of symptoms was four days ago.

History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: No. Um so my skin is a bit cracked in some parts, like kind of cracked, if you see what I mean.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Denies bleeding or discharge from the skin lesions.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: Um have you, have you noticed any uh bleeding or discharge from your skins?
Patient: No.

Doctor: And apart from this, any other symptoms have you noticed? For example, have you noticed any temperature or fevers?
Patient: No. just very itchy. Nothing else.

Doctor: Your chest is OK? No cough, no breathing difficulties?
Patient: No.

Doctor: You're passing urine OK.
Patient: I I think so.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: No recent changes in shower gel or clothing reported.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: So for example, have you changed your uh shower gel, any clothing?
Patient: No I . It's actually like, it's really annoying, because I'm thinking about, maybe I should change something. Because I I haven't, and I don't understand

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Current episode is itchier than prior eczema episodes.
Previous eczema was limited to the arms; current rash also involves the chest and hands.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: my eczema was more like only in the arm. But now it's also on the chest. And in the on the, on the hands as well.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient takes daily showers to ease the itching.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I I have to take like showers every day to be able to, cannot uh ease this itching part, which is very very annoying.

Past_Medical_History.source_text: Um so yes. Uh earlier I was like prescribed for my eczema.

Past_Medical_History.content: History of asthma in the past, resolved.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: Uh, no. I just had asthma in the past. But not anymore.

Medications.source_text:
Doctor: And do you take any regular medications at the moment?
Patient: Uh no.

Medications.content: Purchased and used an over-the-counter steroid cream last night without relief.
Medications.source_text: I've tried a few things. Like I bought a, a steroid cream at the pharmacy last night. But it apparently didn't help, because it's still itching a lot today.

Medications.content: Previously prescribed eczema treatments (cream and shower product) were tried again when symptoms recurred but did not help.
Medications.source_text: at that time yes. That's, those symptoms, like these symptoms appear like, when the symptoms appeared again, I tried those and it didn't work.

Medications.content: Has tried antihistamines recently without benefit.
Medications.source_text: I have tried uh antihistamines, but uh but it didn't really help.

Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Uh so, I live with a few flatmates.
Uh I, yeah I'm I have a full time job.
Uh I work uh at a pharmaceutical company.

Doctor: do you smoke at all?
Patient: No.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Consumes a few beers per week; previously drank more when younger.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: yeah I'd say a few, a few beers per week. Something like this. Nothing, nothing crazy. I used to drink a lot more when I was younger. But it's been, it's been a while.

Physical_Findings.content: Rash mainly affecting the chest and back on clinician observation.
Physical_Findings.source_text: The reason being that you said it was quite itchy. Um it's mainly affecting your chest and your back.

Assessment.source_text: based on everything you mentioned Sarah , I do wonder whether this is a flare-up of your eczema.

Plan_of_Care.source_text:
I wonder whether giving you a stronger prescription of a of a steroid may be beneficial.
Uh, which I'm happy to prescribe to you today.

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe emollients to moisturize the skin and for use in the bath and shower.
Plan_of_Care.source_text:
As well as, I'm going to give you something, some emollients, which helps to moisturize the skin.
Um which use in the bath and shower.

Plan_of_Care.content: Use the steroids and emollients regularly over the next week to ten days.
Plan_of_Care.source_text:
But I think using the steroids and the emollients, um on a regular basis
Uh over the next week to ten days, should hopefully control your symptoms.

Plan_of_Care.content: Consider antihistamines such as loratadine or Piriton to help with itch.
Plan_of_Care.source_text:
Um it's also worth um using antihistamines, which you can sometimes buy over counter.
Things like Loratadine or Piriton, which can help the itchiness of your skin.

I can give you something a little bit stronger today as well.
Um, something like Fexofenadine, which I can give to you today.

Plan_of_Care.content: Keep a diary of potential triggers including clothing and personal care products.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: it's also worth keeping a diary of any triggers which are affecting your symptoms, anything you wear or anything you use, in terms of shower gels or soap.

Follow_up_Information.content: Return for review next week if symptoms do not improve.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: do come back and see me next week, if things don't get better.
